reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I should check the orders and refunds myself, since payouts can't be recalled. I'll start by listing the orders.
Before paying anyone, I need to confirm the refunds in the shared ledger match W2's report, since payouts can't be recalled. I'll list the refunds next.

The ledger's refunds (orders 130 and 133, 8178 and 6783) match W2's report exactly, so I can proceed. Next I'll get the net balance for each customer, starting with acme, rather than computing it myself.
Acme's net balance of 28879 checks out: orders 17595 + 26245 = 43840, minus refunds 8178 + 6783 = 14961, gives 28879. Next I'll get birch's net balance from the tool.
Birch's net balance of 70733 matches its orders (37666 + 33067) with no refunds, so it checks out. Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance from the tool before paying anyone.
Cobalt's net balance of 16841 matches its orders (10547 + 6294) with no refunds. All three balances check out against the orders and refunds, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme at 28879.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch's balance of 70733 matches its orders with no refunds, and I checked it earlier. Next I'll record birch's payout.
Acme and birch are recorded, and cobalt's balance of 16841 matches its orders (10547 + 6294) with no refunds. I'll record cobalt's payout to finish the batch.
All three payouts were recorded successfully. Each balance matched the orders minus the refunds I verified in the ledger, so the batch is complete.
